title: Open Question: Recognition of Switchable Graphs
statement_text: It is not clear whether graphs in the Switchable class (the hereditary class of graphs for which the reconfiguration graph of perfect matchings under flips is connected) can be recognized in polynomial time.
context_text: A flip transforms a perfect matching $M$ into another one by exchanging the edges of an alternating cycle of length four: if $uv,xy\in M$ and $ux,vy\in E(G)$, replace $uv,xy$ by $ux,vy$. The reconfiguration graph of perfect matchings under flips has the perfect matchings of $G$ as vertices, two being adjacent when one is obtained from the other by a flip (flips are the switches of the switch Markov chain used to sample perfect matchings). Dyer, Jerrum and Müller proved that the largest hereditary class of bipartite graphs for which this reconfiguration graph is connected is the class of chordal bipartite graphs; Dyer and Müller generalized this by characterizing the hereditary class of general (non-bipartite) graphs for which it is connected, called Switchable. The authors remark that it is not clear whether this class can be recognized in polynomial time. Their own results concern the decision problem (Perfect Matching Reconfiguration: can one given perfect matching be transformed into another by flips?), which they prove PSPACE-complete for split graphs and for bipartite graphs of bounded bandwidth and maximum degree five, and polynomial for strongly orderable graphs (including interval and strongly chordal graphs), outerplanar graphs and cographs, with linear-length sequences. They also leave open on which classes a shortest reconfiguration sequence can be found in polynomial time.
notes: Stated as a passing remark rather than a labelled problem; paper text is truncated before any concluding open-problems section, so additional conjectures may be present in the full paper.
